title: Tech Tanks and Bonds Pick Up The Slack
summary:
Tech Tanks and Bonds Pick Up The Slack 

             
             
            What began with focus on funding concerns for Coreweave (and, to a lesser degree, a very small handful of other companies) is spreading to bigger tech names today. Mix and match your favorite combo of disappointing earnings, underwhelming guidance, or cautionary tales from analysts. Any combo you choose adds up to massive losses in tech stocks. From there, several avenues lead back to bond buying. At the most superficial level, we can simply say it's a flight to safety. But thinking deeper, an ongoing AI capex slowdown has implications for econ data and corporate bond issuance that would both benefit Treasuries/MBS. Treasuries were 15+bps lower across the curve (even Fed rate expectations) and MBS were up over 5/8ths. Please consider a NASDAQ chart that shows the sell-offs in early June and late July to understand that nothing definitive has happened yet.

title: Another Nice Drop For Rates, Now Near 1-Month Lows
summary: Interest rates continue taking cues from the market rethinking the pace of AI-related growth/spending. Last week's focus was on Coreweave and a few other companies who saw their cost of financing rapidly increase--a sign that investors were starting to worry about future return of capital. One remedy for such worries is to shift money into the safest parts of the bond market such as US Treasuries and mortgage-backed bonds. As demand for those bonds increases, rates fall.   Today was a sharper, broader continuation of the same theme. Disappointing earnings calls and guidance for several big names resulted in heavy selling of tech stocks in addition to ongoing spikes in financing costs for Coreweave and other higher-risk names.   In the simplest terms: tech is tanking and bonds are picking up the slack.  The average top-tier 30yr fixed rate fell 0.10 today to 7.30%. This is the lowest since September 23rd when it was 7.26%.

title: Don't Overthink It. Same Old (New) Story
summary: Oil prices are up. Bond yields are down sharply. If this was early September, that wouldn't make sense. Bonds decoupled from the oil correlation on Fed week and then REALLY decoupled as stronger econ data was priced in, starting with that very weird S&P PMI reaction on Sept 23. Ever since then, yields have been fumbling around in the dark, trying to find a long-term ceiling. Then Coreweave concerns came to the forefront, slowly at first (October 8) and then swiftly last week. Once again today, Coreweave bond drama is directly linked to this morning's sharpest movement toward lower yields.

title: Six MLSs Sue Compass In Listing Fight With Stakes For Purchase Lenders
summary: Six multiple listing services have sued Compass over its demands that they stop penalizing agents who publicly market homes without sharing the listings through the MLS, escalating a dispute over who gets access to for-sale inventory and when.The lawsuit, filed Oct. 21 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, seeks a declaration that the organizations’ cooperation rules comply with federal and state antitrust laws. The plaintiffs also want an injunction barring Compass from bringing or pursuing antitrust claims against them based on those rules.

title: More Buyers Expect Higher Rates. Fewer Would Wait.
summary: Prospective homebuyers are growing more pessimistic about interest rates, and less inclined to wait for relief.In Veterans United Home Loans’ latest survey, 57% expect interest rates to rise over the next year, up from 45% a year earlier. Yet the share who would consider waiting for lower mortgage rates before buying fell from 39% to 32%. Their purchase timelines have changed little, suggesting buyers are reconsidering what waiting might get them rather than rushing to close.

title: Mortgage Rate Lock-In: More High-Rate Loans, Few Signs Of A Thaw
summary: With 30-year mortgage rates above 7%, homeowners holding loans below 4% face a steep financing penalty for moving — and new data show how slowly that obstacle is easing.Nearly half of outstanding mortgages carried rates below 4% in the second quarter, according to Realtor.com’s analysis released Oct. 22. Loans with rates of 6% or higher represented 22.5% of the total, increasing just 0.3 percentage points from the previous quarter.Those figures capture the market through June, before borrowing costs climbed further. Freddie Mac’s average 30-year fixed rate reached 7.40% on Oct. 8 and has remained there, widening the gap for homeowners weighing a replacement mortgage.

title: Investor Homebuying Slows, Small Buyers Claim Biggest Share In 15 Years
summary: Small investors accounted for nearly two-thirds of investor home purchases in the first half of 2026 — and were considerably less likely than the biggest buyers to pay cash, making them a key customer base for originators pursuing investment-property business.Small investors purchased roughly 148,000 homes and represented 66.2% of investor acquisitions, their highest share in at least 15 years, according to Realtor.com’s latest Investor Report, released Oct. 21. Mega-investors purchased approximately 12,700 homes.
